commentPreTextItems.html: 7:30pm Bhuvi will bowl up top, who'll go with him? Will be a challenge against Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma. Out walk the umpires after the fielders are mostly in place. Not Bhuvi but Duffy to begin on IPL debut!. No slips Arjun: "Travishek is brilliant, but will be looking forward to Kishan and Hope Nitish has a nice season! " 7:24pm Thanks, Ashish. A moment's silence being observed right now as a tribute to the lost lives in the stampede last year. A few members from the India women's team are in too, Smriti Mandhana, Shreyanka Patil and Jemimah Rodrigues among others. After the silence, the players walk out for the national anthem. shashank Sinha: "Rajat Patidar's 'We are not defending anything' somehow reminds of Jos Buttler's similar quote before 2023 WC. Hope this turns out different." We are just five minutes from the first ball of IPL 2026. Here's Ekanth back for another stint. Prasanna : "Selection of Abhinandan is interesting. He is selected over Rasikh (6cr) and Mangesh (5.2cr). Also, he was only players retained among 0 IPL cap players (Chikara, Bhandage, Rathee). Big vote of confidence!! " Prasanna : "Expect Devdutt Padikkal to come as impact sub over V. Iyer. Iyer would have started in bowling XI if he was playing as he can chip in with his bowling." 7.15pm What do you think about the two XIs, guys? Surprised that Abhinandan is playing ahead of Rasikh or Mangesh? It could be a risk but there is also the surprise factor with him. The rest of the side is on expected lines, though I am mildly surprised that Bethell has not got a game, particularly with the amount of training he has put in the last two days. A debut game for Jacob Duffy as well. SRH are also on expected lines and do watch out for Salil Arora who was absolutely smoking it at training. SRH might being in either Liam Livingstone or David Payne as their impact player. Playing XIs SRH: 1 Abhishek Sharma, 2 Travis Head, 3 Ishan Kishan (capt & wk), 4 Heinrich Klaasen, 5 Nitish Kumar Reddy, 6 Aniket Verma, 7 Salil Arora, 8 Harsh Dubey, 9 Eshan Malinga, 10 Harshal Patel, 11 Jaydev Unadkat Impact bench: Shivang Kumar, Liam Livingstone, David Payne, R Smaran, Sakib Hussain RCB: 1 Virat Kohli, 2 Phil Salt, 3 Rajat Patidar (capt), 4 Jitesh Sharma (wk), 5 Tim David, 6 Romario Shepherd, 7 Krunal Pandya, 8 Bhuvneshwar Kumar, 9 Abhinandan Singh, 10 Jacob Duffy, 11 Suyash Sharma Impact bench: Devdutt Padikkal, Jacob Bethell, Rasikh Salam, Kanishk Chouhan, Venkatesh Iyer 7pm The RCB-RCB chants are in full flow as it comes to Toss time in Bengaluru: RCB captain Rajat Patidar has the coin, SRH captain Ishan Kishan calls head, it is a tail and RCB will bowl first. Rajat Patidar: It is a season opener, so let's see how the wicket behaves. There are a lot of positives from last season. We are not defending anything, we will win in IPL 2026 as well. [Injuries] There are a lot of good players in the side and the backup players are great as well. All players are fit and the medical staff is looking after the players. [Message to fans] Thank You so much for supporting. We will try and win this again. Ishan Kishan: Feeling good, and we wanted to field first as well. We want to back our instincts. [How to go about the season?] You don't have to start some thing new just because it is IPL. We just want to execute our plans. Obviously Pat is one of the best bowlers, but everyone looks in good touch and I feel we will be on the winning side. [New faces] Salil [Arora] is there, and just want him to keep things simple and trust his instincts. There are two news faces, Jacob and Abhinandan are playing shubham gheeya: "More than scorecard pressure in tournaments of fine margins, it's always a battle of what team you pick to go on the field when you've plenty of options in good shape. That's the area where work behind the screen pays off. Hoping for a cracker of start for both the teams. Expecting RCB to open with Bethell & Shepherd. " Arjun: "The only thing I'm excited is for developing new talents/consistency in kishan and Samson, redemption for Varun. Hope Ro-Ko have brilliant season and Dube turns into a finisher that every team will hope not to face." 6.50pm Pitch report by Kevin Pietersen and Danny Morrison: Not the biggest ground, 65 and 64 metre straight boundaries, 73 downtown, short boundaries behind the wicket. There is grass, some bare patches too but they may not make an impact. You see the sizes of the players and bats, they can clear boundaries. There are a couple of fast bowlers running around. You need to be very very good on this surface. You walk out on a wicket like this as a batter and say .. runs. Win the toss and chase, all day long. 6.40pm Should SRH go with Liam Livingstone or Eshan Malinga? How can RCB fit Jacob Bethell into their XII? What should RCB's overseas combination look like? What is a safe score at the Chinnaswamy... does such a thing even exist? Share us your thoughts. samirD: "Beyond bat and ball, this season is about man-management. Imagine telling Jacob Bethell or Venkatesh Iyer they don't start--not for form, but for balance. That's the real challenge. For teams like RCB and SRH, it's not just picking the XI--it's keeping the rest ready, convinced, and aligned. In a tournament of fine margins, dressing rooms win what scorecards can't." Aditya : "Everyone's saying SRH don't have a good bowling attack but they have plenty of options and all rounders to choose from. I would love to see David Payne, Eshan Malinga and Shivang Kumar bowling this year." Rara: "Think in an era where batting takes importance and 250 are regularly made now, i think whoever bowls well throughout the tournament wins. even when saying that bowling well doesn't win you games, its bowling smarter. " I'd say it is the bowlers who win you matches and tournaments. 6.30pm Thanks, Ekanth and hello everyone. The IPL is back, cricket at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium is back, all is good with the world again. The ground is packed already with just around half and hour to before the toss. The RCB players are wearing No. 11 on their backs as a mark of respect for the people who lost their lives last season in the stampede. The RCB players will also be wearing black armbands for this opening game. Ground updates Duffy is having a bowl on the practice pitches. Krunal is loosening up too. Just over half-hour to go for the toss and the stands are almost full. On that note, it's time to welcome Ashish for his first time this evening. Celine : "Hello, Hello. Excited! Being a loyal RCB fan, I can't believe myself I shall not be supporting Abhisekh Sharma tonight - one of my favorites otherwise!" samirD: "This might actually be decided by the bowling, not the batting. With both sides stacked for runs, the real edge lies in who gets their bowling mix right--new ball control, middle-over containment, and clarity at the death. Between RCB and SRH, it's less about who scores more and more about who concedes smarter" 6:20pm This is the first game at the Chinnaswamy in over ten months. So there is a bit of mystery around how the conditions will play. While it's traditionally a belter and is expected to be the case tonight as well, there could be surprises. Since the last three years, the average score batting first is 194, in the last five games though it's 177. Aneesh: "Hopihg bethell and shepherd play. Because Duffy did not prove himself in india and he is regulary expensive. Play 4 overseas batters/all-rounders with bethell and shepherd able to bowl with venky iyer. Trust rasikh And mangesh to bowl. They will be similar but have more experience in these conditions. Duffy will maybe give 45-runs in his 4-overs but even if rasikh give 55+, those extra 20-runs are better." 6:10pm Chants of RCB grow loud as Kohli walks out. He acknowledges them. He'll be amply supported by the batters. But what about the bowlers, with Hazlewood missing out. Bhuvneshwar is the leader of the attack, he'll have Jacob Duffy and Rasikh Salam. Shepherd is the allrounder who will hold things together. Suyash has Krunal for support. Can they bowl for wickets or will they have to be in a restricting role? Krishna Sumanth: "Everyone says SRH is a weak bowling side. All it takes is a couple of bowlers to be in great form over the next two months. Shivang kumar looks like will be the standout bowler this year." 6pm Now let's get to the weaker parts, the bowling. SRH don't have Cummins, they're likely to bring in Brydon Carse, who can hit 140kph regularly (Our experts seem to disagree with that one). They have the experienced Harshal Patel and Jaydev Unadkat but neither have been strike bowlers in recent IPLs. Harsh Dubey is their spinner with Livingstone an option. What are the names you're looking forward to? Mustafa Moudi : "Though they didnt have a Great Season last year, I truly feel SRH is a Great Team on Paper and have the potential to Win this Season, if their Big Names performs. Wishing them all the Best !!" Sanket : "RCB would miss both Hazelwood and Yash Dayal. RCB's batting has always been great but last time their bowling was also excellent and that played huge part of winning that title. and suddenly at the start of the season you don't have your two biggest contributors of that department so it won't be easy to replace them and that's why Duffy should play here." How can RCB fit Jacob Bethell into their XI? 5:50pm RCB's batting has a problem of plenty. WIth Kohli, Salt, Padikkal and the captain Patidar, and keeper Jitesh the top-five is set. But do they bring in the young but supremely talented Jacob Bethell or stay with Tim David, who finished off innings and games expertly last season. They also bat deep with Krunal Pandya at 8, so it's unlikely for them to play within themselves tonight (which they kinda have to against SRH anyway). Krunal, Ashish informs, has has barely been visible in the training over the last two days. HariharanSPL: "Is Ashish Pant in any way related to Rishabh Pant ? Very curious for it, about a year..." No, and you're not the first to ask. Apparently, Axar Patel started with the same question during an interview. And yes, one of the Pants will be commentating here today After a year of redemption, it's time for Captain Kishan 5:40pm SRH will be without their captain Pat Cummins for the early stages of the tournament to manage his workload. He has been bowling in the team practice but will have to watch from the sidelines as Ishan Kishan captains the side. Kishan has leadership experience with Jharkhand and is coming out hot off a T20 World Cup win. Can he gel SRH like he did his state side and will his batting form continue? Krishna Sumanth: "2016 finalists playing the 2026 opener. it's already a decade! " Preview by Ashish Pant RCB, SRH and Chinnaswamy come together for IPL's opening night 5:30pm The IPL has grown into adulthood and is now taking things up a notch. A first-time winner in RCB brought the tournament alive last time, although the stampede took the sheen out of the win. The Chinnaswamy Stadium has gotten a bit of a makeover, perhaps not enough, but it's ready from the inside to host the season opener. It's RCB vs SRH, two high-scoring sides with slightly weakened bowling line-ups, going against each other. All the ingredients for T20 entertainment are in place, it's time to mix them up and relish.

commentPostTextItems.html: Here's Sampath: Four of Ishan Kishan's six 80-plus scores in the IPL have come in his first innings of the season. No other batter has as many 80-plus scores in their season's first outing. Chris Gayle and AB de Villiers are next with three apiece. Aniket Verma: Very good wicket and feels nice that the team total is beyond 200. I am hoping that we can defend this. [Wicket] It was the last ball, I was trying for a single. The new ball is skidding, so i think that will help our team. 9.27pm SRH lost three wickets early, but then came a solid stand between Kishan and Klaasen and then they lost wickets in a cluster again. But thanks to an Aniket Verma cameo, SRH have gone past 200. Is this enough? One can't be sure, but there was some terrific cricket on display, that is for certain. Jacob Duffy, playing his first IPL game of the season, ran through the SRH top order removing Abhishek, Head and Reddy inside the powerplay. Kishan and Klaasen then put on 97 of 53 balls to arrest the slide. Klaasen fell to a contentious decision, but Kishan continued on his merry way, thrashing 80 off 38 balls. His innings was cut short by a Salt stunner. It seemed at that stage that SRH might fall short but Aniket thrashed 43 off 18 to take SRH past 200. Will this be enough? Join Ekanth in a bit to find out Shadow-Shell: "Kohli might've taken Aniket. But it definitely had a cost. That could be the difference " Rk: "Bhuvi is ageing like a fine wine. Bowling under 8RPO at Chinnaswamy that too bowling in powerplay and death is next to impossible but Bhuvi does it with ease." Srividya Raamad: "After those 3 quick wickets, SRH would be glad to have crossed 200 ! " Jugilee : "This may historically be a chasing venue but 201 looks a defendable score ! "

commentTextItems.html: That's that! Defending champions start IPL 2026 with a statement win. At the halfway mark, the question was is 200 enough? The way RCB went about the chase, even 250 wasn't going to be enough tonight. They have galloped past the 202 target in 15.4 overs and with some style. Kohli ends the game with another boundary. Slower short ball outside off, he ramps this over short third and ends with an unbeaten 69 off 38. RCB win by six wickets with 26 balls to spare.

commentPostTextItems.html: What a start to IPL 2026 as RCB obliterate SRH, chasing 202 in 15.4 overs. What seemed like a tricky score at the halfway mark ended up being well short by the end of it. SRH have a lot of catching up to do and RCB are playing like defending champions. That will be it from us tonight, thanks for tuning in. Thanks for all your feedback, we will be back nice and early tomorrow for the MI-KKR game so do tune in. Till then, this is me Ashish, signing off on behalf of Ekanth, Chandan and Sudeep. Ciao! Jacob Duffy is the player of the match: Awesome, hell of a way to start the campaign. Great win. [Doing the Hazlewood role] I am just keeping the big fellow's seat warm. I just wanted to bowl the hard lengths, just keep the ball there. Even better that I got to walk off the field after seven overs. We talked about the lengths and stuff, what works here. Just build on what Josh did. [Learning from the T20 WC] I am sick of bowling to Abhishek for sure. Haven't seen such bounce in India before as we saw here. But that was the case today. [Four overs on the bounce] Just Rajat said you go and I happily obliged, When the ball is hard and new is the best time to bowl on this surface. RCB captain, Rajat Patidar: [Happy?] 100% The way boys played and this was a season opener. Everyone chipped in and did the job. [Powerplay bowling] Duffy was playing his first game and the way he played and the wickets he took were the turning point. [Quick batting] Not a policy, we assessed the wicket and it was good. Padikkal and Kohli's innings were the base. [On Kohli] No words for him. The way he goes in, the team is chasing. He is the No. 1 batter. [Catching] That was a terrific catch by Salt. Even I was surprised but he is a great fielder. [His batting] I wanted to create a lot of impact and I wanted to chase this quickly. I just wanted to have a lot of impact. Presentation time Shadow-Shell: "So SRH was atleast 50 short" Hari: "Quietly, after 18 odd years, looks like RCB are turning Chinnaswamy into a fortress. It used to be reverse everytime with RCB on the receiving end but not today." Rajkumar Lingav: "RCB made a statement here: dominated, finished strong, and boosted that NRR in style!" Virat Kohli: It was good to get back out there. The last game I played was the final last year but I think the way I batted in the one-day series quite recently really helped me to stay in that same kind of momentum. I wasn't playing shots that I don't usually play so I knew as long as I have the rhythm and I've put enough work physically behind the scenes with my fitness, things should come together nicely and tonight was another chance to start strong and to build on this. [Playing one format] The kind of scheduling that we've had over the last 15 years and the amount of cricket I've played, for me there was always a risk of getting burnt out rather than being undercooked. So these breaks helped me immensely. I stay fresh, I stay excited. Whenever I come back to play, it's 120%. I'm not coming back underprepared. In fact, the extra rest helps me to mentally freshen up. And as long as you're physically fit and you're excited mentally, all those things come together nicely and then you're able to contribute for the team's cause and that's what you want to do as a player. You don't want to hold on to a spot. You want to keep performing and keep putting in the work for the team. [On Padikkal] Outstanding knock. Right from the word go. I had plans of going aggressive in the powerplay, but when I saw him play, I was like, keep putting him back on strike and hit the odd boundary here and there. So, yeah, he completely took the game away from the opposition and I told him that one shot he hit off a slower ball over mid-on for six. At that time, I told him just keep going on. I mean, you're hitting the ball amazingly well and just keep pushing it and take the game away from the opposition. His head positions, his balance, absolutely world-class. SRH captain, Ishan Kishan: The wicket played well after the first three to four overs. We lost early wickets and we have to take care of that. The wicket got better in the second innings. We have to be smarter with our shot selection. [Bowlers] You have to give credit to the batters, especially Virat bhai. Very important to get his wicket. We have to work harder, these mistakes are acceptable in the first game, but we have to be cautious. [Captaincy] I enjoyed it a lot, but it is IPL sometimes there are nerves but we will get better as a team. If we win games going ahead, it will be even better. 11.03pm Virat Kohli has his arms up in delight, he blows a kiss to his wife Anushka Sharma in the stands. He then gives a hug to Patidar who has played his part in this chase. All smiles in the RCB dugout, who have started IPL 2026 in some style. Phil Salt was dismissed early but Devdutt Padikkal and displayed some of the most cleanest ball striking you will ever see. He smashed a fifty off 21 balls, his fastest in the IPL and finished with 61 off 26. David Payne on IPL debut struck twice in two balls but that was a little too late. Patidar smashed 31 off 12 balls while David and Kohli remained unbeaten. Kohli finished on 69* off 38 balls as RCB won with lots to spare.
